subject: Nanotechnology
title: Lipid Self-Assembly
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Lipid Self-Assembly.

hook.text: Drop lipids in water and they spontaneously form spheres — liposomes that look just like tiny cell membranes.

buildup.text: Lipid molecules have a water-loving head and water-fearing tails — the hydrophobic effect drives them to assemble.

discovery.text: The shape of the assembly depends on lipid geometry — cylinders form bilayers, cones form micelles, inverted cones form tubes.

twist.text: Liposomes are not just biology — they are drug delivery vehicles. Doxil, the first nano drug, is a liposome.

climax.text: COVID mRNA vaccines use lipid nanoparticles — self-assembled lipid shells that protect and deliver the RNA payload.

punchline.text: Lipids assemble themselves into medicine — biology's simplest trick saves millions.

quiz.question: What determines whether lipids form micelles, bilayers, or tubes?
options: The temperature of the solution only
The geometric shape of the lipid molecule, with cylinders forming bilayers and cones forming micelles
The color of the lipid determines the structure
